## Join

**[Open the membership form](https://forms.gle/yhXSwWUDRqEu8BFNA)**. It takes about five minutes and needs no sign-in. You choose whether you appear on the public map, which details are shown, and whether you join the mailing list.

New entries appear on the map once a curator has checked them, usually within a few days.

## Your personal link

After you submit, the confirmation page shows an **"Edit your response"** link. This is your personal link: bookmark it. We also email it to you.

Open it at any time to change your answers. Changes appear on the map within about 10 minutes.

Lost it, and our email never arrived? Write to [rdn.projectbase@gmail.com](mailto:rdn.projectbase@gmail.com) and we'll help.

## Photo

Every email we send you has a link to the **photo form**, where you can add, change or remove a photo. Google asks you to sign in to upload one. Uploading a photo means it's shown with your entry on the map.

## Leave {#leave}

- **With your personal link:** open it, tick **Leave the network** on the last page, and submit. This takes effect straight away.
- **No link?** Use the **[leave form](LEAVE_FORM_URL)**. A curator confirms the request, usually within a few days.

We then remove you from the map and the mailing list, delete your entry and any photo, and email you to confirm.

## If our emails don't arrive {#emails}

Our emails are sent automatically by the system that runs RDN membership, so they come from the network's own account, **rdn.projectbase@gmail.com** (sender name "Response Diversity Network (membership)"), rather than from a person. Some organisations' email systems treat automated messages like this with suspicion and may move them to junk or hold them in quarantine.

To help them reach you, add rdn.projectbase@gmail.com to your contacts or safe senders before you submit. If nothing arrives within an hour, check your junk folder and your organisation's quarantine. In Microsoft 365, that's the quarantine notification email or [security.microsoft.com/quarantine](https://security.microsoft.com/quarantine).

You don't need the email to manage your entry: the "Edit your response" link on the confirmation page is the same personal link.

## Privacy {#privacy}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft for review.** Check this notice with the University of Zurich data protection office before launch.
:::

**Who is responsible.** The Response Diversity Network (RDN). Contact: Owen Petchey, University of Zurich, [owen.petchey@uzh.ch](mailto:owen.petchey@uzh.ch).

**What we collect.** The answers you give in the membership form:

- your name and email address;
- your institution, city and country;
- an optional website;
- your research interests;
- your research attributes, such as career stage and the systems you study;
- an optional photo (added with the photo form);
- your consent choices.

**Why.** To run the network: to keep a member list, to show a public map of members (only if you agree), and to add you to the mailing list (only if you ask). The legal basis is your consent (Swiss revFADP; EU GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)).

**What is public.** Only if you tick "show me on the public map", and only the details you choose. Your location is shown at city level, never as an address. The full record is never published. The map page also shows overall counts, such as the number of members per country, continent and career stage. These counts include all members but never name anyone, and countries with fewer than three members are not listed.

**Photos.** If you upload a photo (and appear on the map), we publish a small copy (about 400 pixels wide). Google re-creates the copy from your upload, which removes hidden data stored in photo files, such as where the photo was taken. The copy is publicly viewable by anyone who has its link. Your original upload stays private.

**Where your data is stored.** In Google Forms, Google Sheets and Google Drive in RDN's Google account. This means it is stored on Google's servers, which may be outside Switzerland or the EU. If you use the photo form, Google also knows which Google account submitted it. A small number of RDN organisers can access the data. The mailing list is run separately by the list manager.

**How long we keep it.** Until you leave. When you leave, we delete your entry, your stored form response and your photos.

**Your rights.** You can see, correct or delete your data at any time with your personal update link, or by emailing us. You can withdraw consent at any time. You may also complain to the Swiss FDPIC or to your EU data protection authority.
